findings.title: B's post-cancel state is only recorded as prose, unlike post_cancel_A
findings.message: B's post-cancel state — the core assertion of this scenario ("Unsaved B must survive Cancel") — is recorded only as prose inside native_sequence (line 11), while A gets a structured post_cancel_A object (lines 43-51). Anything parsing this JSON to verify results cannot check B's note count, Edited status, toolbar state, or the exact Unicode payload after the Cancel; it would have to regex free-text narrative.
findings.suggestion: Add a post_cancel_B sibling mirroring post_cancel_A, e.g. "post_cancel_B": { "window": "Vellum Documents — B", "notes": 8, "status": "Edited", "title": "Unsaved B must survive Cancel", "body": "B remains dirty: café 日本語\nDo not lose this eighth note.", "toolbar_enabled": true }.
findings.evidence: "B Cancel selected; eight notes and exact unsaved Unicode payload remained, toolbar enabled, Edited status",

findings.title: Conflicting B note counts: "seven notes" vs "eight notes"
findings.message: Line 12 records B's pre-closeout primary hash "with seven notes", but every other record for B in this file says eight notes: "B dirtied to eight notes" (line 5), "eight notes and exact unsaved Unicode payload remained" (line 11), saved_closeout.B.notes = 8 (line 30), and the n11 body calls itself "this eighth note" (line 37). As written, the verification record contradicts itself: a reader cannot tell whether the hash covers the 7-note on-disk fixture before the unsaved eighth note was saved, or whether "seven" is a transcription error in the evidence for a data-loss test.
findings.suggestion: State which artifact the hash covers. If it is the on-disk file before the fixture-preserving save, make the memory-vs-disk distinction explicit so the count discrepancy cannot be misread as data loss or a recording error.

findings.title: "saved/dirty states" leaves the A/B state mapping implicit
findings.message: The shorthand "saved/dirty states" does not say which document ended in which state, and because the preceding paragraph says B was subsequently saved normally, a reader cannot tell whether "saved/dirty" refers to the moment of cancellation or to the final closeout. Since this file is the human-readable summary of a precision check, the mapping should be explicit.
findings.suggestion: State the per-document state explicitly, e.g. "...in their expected states at cancellation (A saved, B dirty), with the later B Save explicitly separate from cancellation acceptance."

findings.title: Overbroad "nothing changed" disclaimer contradicts the described saves
findings.message: The blanket disclaimer "No app code, artifact, personal notebook or global setting changed" conflicts with the test description: A was saved through the Quit prompt and "B was then saved normally", so the synthetic A/B fixture notebook files on disk did change during this item. If "artifact" is meant to cover the fixture data, the claim is inaccurate; if it means build artifacts, it is ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Qualify the disclaimer so it clearly excludes the fixture notebooks that were written by the test, e.g. "No app code, build artifact, personal notebook or global setting changed; the synthetic fixture notebooks themselves were saved as described."
